Laravel app. Packages: inertiajs/inertia-laravel v2, laravel/fortify v1, laravel/framework v12, laravel/prompts v0, laravel/wayfinder v0, laravel/boost v2, laravel/mcp v0, laravel/pail v1, laravel/pint v1, laravel/sail v1, pestphp/pest v4, phpunit/phpunit v12.

This project has domain-specific skills available. You MUST activate the relevant skill whenever you work in that domain—don't wait until you're stuck.
- `wayfinder-development`: activate when referencing backend routes in frontend components, importing from `@/actions` or `@/routes`, calling Laravel routes from TypeScript, or using Wayfinder route functions.
- `pest-testing`: activate for tests, assertions, Livewire/browser tests, failures, datasets, mocks, or when testing is mentioned.

Follow existing conventions; check sibling files and reuse components. Use descriptive names. Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change the application's dependencies without approval. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work. Unit and feature tests are more important. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user. Be concise. If frontend changes aren't visible, ask whether to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev`.

Use Laravel Boost tools: `list-artisan-commands` for Artisan options; `get-absolute-url` for project URLs; `tinker` for PHP debugging/Eloquent queries; `database-query` for read-only database access; `database-schema` before migrations/models; `browser-logs` for recent browser logs only. Search docs before code changes using `search-docs`; use broad, simple, topic-based queries, multiple queries where useful, and omit package names. It returns version-specific docs. Query syntax supports stemming, AND words, `"exact phrases"`, mixed terms, or query arrays.

Use curly braces for control structures. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion; avoid empty public constructors (private is allowed). Declare explicit return types and parameter types. Prefer TitleCase enum keys, PHPDoc over inline comments (comments only for exceptionally complex logic), and useful array shapes.

Herd serves `https?://[kebab-case-project-dir].test`. You must not run any commands to make the site available via HTTP(S). It is always available through Laravel Herd.

Every change must be programmatically tested. Write a new test or update an existing test, then run the affected tests to make sure they pass. Run the minimum needed: `php artisan test --compact` with a filename or filter.

Inertia: components in `resources/js/pages` (unless `vite.config.js` specifies otherwise); use `Inertia::render()` rather than Blade. ALWAYS use `search-docs` for version-specific Inertia documentation. Check docs before using v1/v2 features; deferred props need an animated/pulsing skeleton empty state.

Laravel: create files with `php artisan make:` and `--no-interaction`, using correct options; generic PHP classes use `php artisan make:class`. Use Eloquent relationships with return types; prefer ORM over `DB::`/raw queries, eager-load to prevent N+1, and use query builder for complex operations. New models need useful factories/seeders; ask about extras and check `php artisan make:model` options. APIs default to versioned Eloquent Resources unless existing conventions differ. Use Form Requests (rules and custom messages); check sibling rule style. Use built-in auth/a
